## Principal finding and correction to the premise

P/config/scenarios/scenario-uneven-multisched-01.json:184–196 defines an ENABLED diesel
block: 20 MW, start delay 3600 s. P/api/schemas.py:2484–2492 materializes that block
into `diesel_units` during ScenarioSpec validation. P/runtime/scenario_factory.py:1022–1045
constructs runtime modules from `diesel_units`, not from the block alone.
P/study_harness/executor.py:262–273 loads raw JSON and applies a turbine fuel overlay
without that schema materialization. Thus the study has zero diesel units; the
catalogue/app has one. This is present BEFORE tick 1, not introduced by RunManager.
Printed floors are in T/A.floor0.json, B.floor0.json and C.floor0.json:

```json
{
  "A": {
    "diesel_worst_case_sync_s": 0.0,
    "bess_floor_mwh": [
      0.0
    ],
    "dynamic_commitment_mode": "baseline"
  },
  "B": {
    "diesel_worst_case_sync_s": 0.0,
    "bess_floor_mwh": [
      0.0
    ],
    "dynamic_commitment_mode": "informed"
  },
  "C": {
    "diesel_worst_case_sync_s": 3660.0,
    "bess_floor_mwh": [
      76.25
    ],
    "dynamic_commitment_mode": "ABSENT"
  }
}
```

The 76.25 MWh floor exceeds this scenario's 60 MWh usable battery capacity
(P/config/scenarios/scenario-uneven-multisched-01.json:181). The source formula is
P/core/dispatch.py:505–528: max(depth reserve, 2.5 × 30 MW × 3660 s / 3600).
The resulting normal-dispatch BESS ceiling is zero, unlike the study's 29 MW.
No constant, floor, or scenario was tuned to obtain these findings.

The earlier `67f2516c…51ac` hash was NOT the unmodified catalogue baseline_runner
hash: tools/dr_isl/PHASE_2B_STOP1_REPORT.md:34–42,89–100 explicitly describes a
study-prepared replay adapter through the runner. The unmodified runner now hashes
`bd125c313284ddfcb7f5a5e1112b95ab25cc82a9a731273cb050a7a14e3d31a9`.
The old FULL hash and 15.267058272851246 MWh are both reproduced below by applying
the existing ScenarioSpec validation to the prepared conventional study arm.
This contradicts treating the old hash as a plain catalogue run; it does not
contradict the printed energy result. Neither configuration was adjusted to force
the expected 4.79/0.37 result.

Metric arithmetic is P/study_harness/metrics.py:275–280 for ALL four.
A/B pass the unmodified fuel-model guard. C/D do NOT pass that guard:
`FuelModelAbsentError('synchronized turbine(s) have no fuel model: gt-spin-01')`
at P/study_harness/metrics.py:261–272. Actual frame config has fuel=None
(P/runtime/scenario_factory.py:834–842), unlike the study's aero overlay
(P/runtime/phase2b_reference.py:41–49). No fuel model was injected into C/D.
To report ENERGY despite this independent guard, T/diagnose.py:metrics explicitly
re-collects a diagnostic tick projection with turbine_units=[] through the SAME
MetricsCollector.add, preserving every energy and fuel-telemetry field; it only
skips the missing-model eligibility guard. This is NOT a valid fuel-study result
or a passing finalize(). The zero turbine counter is not a claim of zero fuel.
Fuel is reported in MMBtu for modelled turbines and gallons for diesel, not summed
across incompatible units. Diesel burn source is P/core/diesel_fleet.py:365–385.
A/B have no FC or diesel generation; C/D have unmodelled GT fuel plus diesel burn.

The summation operation order is intentionally identical to MetricsCollector.add:
MW × (5.0/3600.0). Summing (MW × 5.0)/3600.0 independently yields
15.267058272851239 or 4.794773293941511 due to floating arithmetic, not a run delta.

Repeatability: full fieldwise comparison after only the four contract exclusions
finds zero differing ticks and zero differing fields within A1/A2, B1/B2, C1/C2,
D1/D2 (T/comparisons.json, first four entries).
C equals NEITHER A nor B. D and C have identical energy, operating trajectories
and all hashed fields except run_id (1440 ticks): route-generated run identity
versus baseline runner identity. With the SAME route run_id supplied to the factory,
the C-route-id control hash is exactly D's hash and fieldwise difference is zero:

## 1d.3 — First divergence and turbine/BESS split

EARLIEST internal/configuration difference is tick 0: raw harness lacks a
materialized diesel fleet and has no diesel reserve. The initial potential future
power constraint is already different (floors printed above). A/B also intentionally
have different controller modes, GT fuel models and scheduler/replay mechanism.

Earliest full TickResult difference is tick 1, not tick 9, when comparing all
contract fields: run_id, diesel_enabled/fuel/runtime metadata, source/fuel reporting
and RunManager enrichments differ. The complete first-tick difference is in the
appendix comparison A-trace versus C-trace. The FIRST different measured
GT/BESS dispatch and SoC in the compared demand/generation channels is tick 9,
sim_time 45.0 s. Do not generalize the earlier selected-field claim into full-stream equality.

### Tick-9 call chain and literal values
- RunContext.step, P/runtime/run_manager.py:1803–1844:
  _advance_internal_slurm (:1580), _apply_due_events (:1571), optional forecast
  controller.evaluate, drain_operator_commands, SimClock(dt=5,rate=0),
  evaluate_tick. A baseline evaluate exits without forecast actions at
  P/runtime/turbine_commitment.py:793–797; C has no controller. No difference in
  the forecast/advisory loop is needed to explain this tick.
- P/core/simulation_core.py:1205–1219: A takes the frozen replay pair; C takes
  live scheduler demand. Both have compute=18.85204445111111 MW, cooling=0,
  total demand=18.85204445111111 MW at tick 9 (printed tick rows below).
- P/core/simulation_core.py:1642–1673: synchronized minimums total 17.5 MW,
  incremental GT headroom=32.5 MW. Residual economic demand=1.3520444511111087 MW.
- DispatchArbitrator.diesel_worst_case_sync_s, P/core/dispatch.py:479–503:
  A returns 0; C returns 0 start offset + 3600 startup + 60 residual ramp = 3660.
- DispatchArbitrator.soc_floor_mwh, P/core/dispatch.py:505–528:
  depth term=0 in both, diesel term A=0/C=76.25 MWh, final floor A=0/C=76.25.
- BessModule.bridging_available_mw, P/core/asset_modules.py:1595–1623:
  30 MW rated minus 1 MW grid-forming reserve = 29 MW in both.
  BessModule.deliverable_energy_mwh (:1625–1630), passed the reserve floor by
  P/core/simulation_core.py:1707–1723: A has energy available; C has NONE above
  76.25 MWh even at 100% SoC (battery usable capacity 60 MWh).
- _cost_ranked_dispatch_allocations, P/core/simulation_core.py:777–839:
  same catalogue marginal-cost ordering, but BESS availability A=29/C=0.
  Inputs/returns are printed from trace records below.
- P/core/simulation_core.py:1736–1739: A planned BESS=1.3520444511111087,
  GT target=17.5; C planned BESS=0, GT target=18.85204445111111.
- apply_loading at P/core/loading.py:138–158, called from
  P/core/simulation_core.py:1781–1783: A fleet=17.5, C fleet=18.85204445111111,
  dt=5. Sequential allocation P/core/loading.py:76–98 yields the first two
  synchronized unit outputs A=[8.75,8.75], C=[10.102044451111109,8.75].
  Unit ramp ceiling is 0.5 MW/s × 5 s=2.5 MW, so this movement is feasible.
  TurbineModule.set_output P/core/asset_modules.py:1030–1055 writes the returned
  achieved values; no overwritten/stale setpoint is needed to explain them.

### Causal classification for this trace
(a) Configuration difference: yes — study controllers/fuel/replay are intentional
overrides, but missing schema diesel materialization is not merely choosing
baseline versus informed. It removes an enabled source and its reserve constraint.
(b) RunManager-only runtime behavior: NOT the cause of this energy divergence.
Same-input A-manager/B-manager/C-direct controls retain the same curtailment,
fuel/energy and operating trajectories; only listed runtime telemetry differs.
(c) Genuine defect: study input-normalization/materialization bypass.
(d) Other: run identity and post-physics enrichment explain raw hash differences,
not the 10.472284978909736 MWh curtailment difference.
No evidence here identifies wall-clock/async ordering, advisory autonomy,
corruption, solar sync or persistence as the cause of the tick-9 split.

## 1d.4 — Canonical customer path and displayed values

For an UNMODIFIED selected scenario, full 7200 s, no generator or BESS overrides:
- F/components/RunControlBar.tsx:237–252 POSTs /runs with scenario_id, speed,
  duration and only explicit operator overrides. It does NOT select a study arm.
  This scenario has no generator_config preset in its JSON; if an operator has
  the live generator running, the override can intentionally change the run.
- P/api/routes/scenarios.py:1454–1466 validates then seeds the ScenarioSpec;
  store._seed serializes via model_dump_json at :123–137.
- P/api/routes/runs.py:280–291 reads the stored spec; :659–691 builds via the
  normal factory and starts RunManager.
- P/api/schemas.py:1689–1696 defaults turbine_commitment_mode to disabled.
  Factory:1924–1944 creates no forecast commitment controller for disabled.
  Therefore the app default is LEGACY/DISABLED commitment, neither study informed
  nor the explicitly named study conventional arm. C-baseline-mode happened to
  have identical TickResult hash on this input; that equality does not make the
  configurations or conceptual policies identical.

There is no located GS-DES-SSH-001 text establishing equality with arbitrary
UI-default runs. Located spec-reference evidence:
docs/addendum-h-phase2b-results/s1-metrics-replay.md:1 names GS-DES-SSH-001;
P/scripts/run_study_harness_s1.py:132 labels the study that way.
The executable contract is explicit in P/study_harness/executor.py:321–354:
select baseline/informed, replace live schedulers with shared replay, use the
same engine. P/runtime/phase2b_reference.py:44 says the fuel overlay remains in
the study layer. This supports a controlled two-arm engine study, NOT an
assertion that its output equals the default app topology/configuration.

UI vs metric distinction:
- The app route's FULL tick stream integrates to 15.267058272851246 MWh using
  the study energy collector (D1=D2); not 4.79477329394151 or 0.3700526648755099.
- P/runtime/run_manager.py:575–578 sends p_dispatch_curtailed_mw in tick payloads
  rounded to four decimals. Raw TickResults are used above; integration of rounded
  frontend payloads need not reproduce every last decimal.
- A literal source search of the SERVED frontend F for dispatch_curtailment_mwh,
  p_dispatch_curtailed_mw, “Stranded Power”, stranded found ONLY
  F/types.ts:294 (p_dispatch_curtailed_mw declaration), not a rendered cumulative
  MWh display. Therefore this audit does NOT claim the app currently DISPLAYS
  a 15.27 MWh cumulative total. It is the energy in the app-path tick stream.
  The quoted 4.79/0.37 are reproducible STUDY results, not the default app result.
  No customer-facing Stranded Power Report document was altered or approved here.

## 1d.5 — Classification, scope and fix directions (no code)

| Finding | Classification | Evidence / direction |
|---|---|---|
| Enabled diesel block disappears in raw study build | Genuine HARNESS defect: missing common schema materialization | executor:262–273 versus schemas:2484–2492 and factory:1022–1045. Fix direction: prepare study inputs through the same canonical scenario validation/materialization boundary before probing and constructing both arms. |
| Baseline/informed controller and aero fuel overlay versus app disabled/frame | Expected, explicit study configuration differences | executor:321–326; phase2b_reference:41–49; schema:1689–1696; factory:834–842. Keep these overrides explicit in study identity/reporting; no controller/fuel fix is diagnosed here. |
| Same input direct-step vs RunManager full hash unequal | Expected runtime enrichment and hash coverage, not an observed energy-dispatch defect | manager:2715–2788,2932–3030,3090–3155; exact differing fields in appendix. No physics fix supported. |
| Historical 67f… called plain runner path | Historical comparison/provenance error, not a fault in persisted baseline_runner | STOP1 report:34–42,89–100 and normalized-baseline control reproduces full hash exactly. Fix direction for reporting: distinguish adapted study replay from unmodified catalogue runs and compare resolved inputs before presenting parity claims. |
| C/D “total fuel” unavailable | Missing frame fuel model, not zero fuel consumption | factory:834–842 and metrics:261–272. No fuel calibration or model change is authorized by this read-only phase. |

RunManager defect: NOT SUPPORTED by same-input energy/operating comparisons.
Persisted runner defect causing this dispatch divergence: NOT SUPPORTED; it
correctly follows the seeder path. Two-phase normalization exposes the defect
in the harness input path. A partial “fix” that changes only dispatch ordering or
the reserve floor would address a symptom on the wrong layer; none was attempted.

Scope must distinguish ACTUAL harness support from a direct-step proxy.
P/study_harness/executor.py:45–54 only supports the base demo and declared
Addendum-H reference IDs. All five requested regression IDs raise
UnsupportedScenarioError through the actual harness selector:

fieldwise identical. Hybrid-ai is NOT: the same missing diesel materialization
changes actual outputs, shortfall and curtailment. 100mw-fuel-cell-bess-diesel
also loses the runtime diesel unit(s) on the raw path; in this recorded window
its changed fields are diesel_enabled, initial fuel/runtime and active-target
metadata, not output/SoC/unserved. Exact per-scenario field lists appear in the
appendix. Do not generalize “no output delta in this window” into absence of the
materialization bug. Source scope is raw-factory versus seeder-bound factory.

## Limitations and observed diagnostic-script issue
- D is the permitted in-process actual-route equivalent, not a signed-in UI run.
- The actual study harness does not support the five scope IDs; matched direct-step
  controls and raw-factory controls are explicitly named instead.
- C/D lack modeled turbine fuel. Energy-only collector projection is explicit above;
  no total all-source fuel estimate or passing fuel finalizer is invented.
- Initial diagnostic post-processing used `physical_balance["passed"]`, but the
  raw dataclass JSON contains `closes`, not the passed property. It raised
  KeyError('passed') AFTER D1 completed and was saved (T/diagnose.log).
  T/diagnose.py was corrected only in scratch to inspect closes; D1 was read back
  from its saved stream, NOT rerun. D2 then completed. No application file changed.
- Main full-context snapshots initially omitted dynamically attached dataclass
  members. The new no-step snapshot includes those members; it is not a new run.
- The richer nine-tick traces use the exact same inputs as completed runs and
  record no parameter mutation; they are diagnostics, not scenario modifications.
- The unchanged baseline runner automatically wrote its engine-owned kube debug
  CSV at /tmp/kube_debug_scenario-uneven-multisched-01.csv. The retained copy is
  relocated under T for the final scratch inventory; all other new diagnostics
  redirect that standard runtime debug path into T.
- No security/SEO scan, test-suite rerun, deployment or fix was started.
